messages.text: Monday, September 28 · Canton, Michigan
Autumn air, a full moon rising, and local histories on display
A partly cloudy autumn day offers a high near 76°F. Local history is on display in Ypsilanti, while science explores the early assembly of our own galaxy.
Expect partly cloudy skies today with a high near 76°F and a low around 51°F.
Sunrise is at 7:28 AM, sunset at 7:20 PM, with a full moon 96.9% illuminated.
Local happenings and cultural notes

In Ypsilanti, the YDL-Superior is featuring the Ypsi Farmers & Gardeners Oral History Exhibit, offering a free look at local food growers. For music lovers, Spiral Galaxy performs at Trinosophes in Detroit at 7:30 PM.
Mark your calendar for September 30, which is My Birthday and Patrick's Birthday.
Ann Arbor's fiscal plans and U-M's cancer research

Ann Arbor City Council has approved a spending plan for funds from a downtown property sale, allocating $14.2 million to $17.4 million across 12 projects. The University of Michigan has also established a $10 million center to advance soundwave cancer treatments.
Tomorrow's events and learning opportunities
Tomorrow offers a fireside chat on Black Reading Month at Howard Family Bookstore in Detroit at 6 PM, and an interactive workshop on AI for everyday use at Farmington Library at 6 PM.
Space telescope finds ancient galactic collision

NASA's Hubble telescope has identified evidence of an ancient collision with a dwarf galaxy that shaped the Milky Way's early assembly. Additionally, NASA's Starling satellites have demonstrated GPS-free autonomous navigation in orbit.
The next Starship orbital flight attempt is estimated no earlier than September 18, 2026.
A quiet afternoon can hold a universe of discovery.
Tuesday, September 29 · Canton, Michigan
Overcast skies and a warm breeze greet September's end

Tuesday brings an overcast but warm feel with a high near 75°F. The day's local thread centers on a significant local funding announcement for first responders, while science offers a glimpse into NASA's autonomous satellite navigation.
Today will be overcast with a high near 75°F and a low around 49°F.
The sun rises at 7:29 AM and sets at 7:19 PM, with the moon appearing as a Waning Gibbous at 91.9% illumination.
Evening events in Detroit and Ann Arbor

In Detroit, catch the premiere of "Etched In Pavement" at the Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History at 7:00 PM, or enjoy comedy with Colin Mochrie & Brad Sherwood at Sound Board at 7:30 PM. Ann Arbor offers music by Shwayze at the Blind Pig at 9:00 PM.
Tomorrow, September 30, marks My Birthday and Patrick's Birthday.
First Responder Mental Health Initiative Receives Substantial Funding

A statewide initiative to support first responders will receive $1.044 million in funding. The funds are designated for Frontline Strong Together to aid police officers, firefighters, EMS personnel, correctional officers, and 9-1-1 dispatchers.
Tomorrow's local happenings and upcoming events

Tomorrow, September 30, consider Alexis N. Nelson discussing "Foraging a Better Future" at the U-M School of Environment and Sustainability, or attend the "Community Table" event on black walnuts in Ann Arbor at 6:00 PM.
Satellites Achieve GPS-Free Navigation and Lunar Landing Tests

NASA's Starling satellites have successfully demonstrated autonomous navigation using onboard cameras and a catalog of space objects, eliminating the need for GPS. Additionally, NASA has initiated its most flight-relevant tests for lunar landing plume behavior.
The next Starship launch is estimated to be no earlier than September 18, 2026, though this is an independent estimate and not an official SpaceX schedule.
Seek out a moment of quiet focus in the day's offerings.
